title: Three Horizons Vision
subtitle: You oscillate between being too focused on today's execution and too lost in long-term
useWhen: vision. Strategic planning sessions drift into fantasy. Daily operations crowd out anything beyond this week. You need a framework that holds all three time horizons at once.
howToUse: McKinsey's Three Horizons framework, developed in the late 1990s, organises strategic thinking across three simultaneous timeframes: Horizon 1 (12 months - defend and optimise your core business), Horizon 2 (1–3 years - develop and scale emerging opportunities), and Horizon 3 (3–5 years - create options for future growth). The framework does not suggest sequential attention - all three horizons require investment and attention simultaneously, in different proportions based on company stage. Applied personally, it becomes a powerful vision tool for founders designing their own trajectory.
steps: Map your current allocation of time and energy across the three horizons most founders are trapped in H1.
H3 ideas require protection from H1 urgency, they will never survive if they must justify themselves on H1 metrics.
Build an H2 pipeline even when H1 is working well, H1 success is temporary without H2 in development.
Review your Three Horizons map quarterly, the business changes faster than annual reviews can track. Plan three futures simultaneously without losing the present
origin: McKinsey & Company — Three Horizons framework, Baghai, Coley & White, 1999
promptBody:
Act as a strategic planning advisor using McKinsey's Three Horizons framework.
My business                             :  [DESCRIBE YOUR CURRENT CORE BUSINESS]
Stage                                          :  [REVENUE RANGE AND GROWTH RATE]
Current strategic priorities  :  [WHAT YOU ARE FOCUSED ON NOW]
Map my Three Horizons:
HORIZON 1 (This year) :
What is the core business I must protect and optimise?
Key metrics to defend. Main threats to manage.
HORIZON 2 (1–3 years) :
What 2–3 adjacent opportunities should I be developing?
What experiments should I be running now?
What would need to be true for each to become H1?
HORIZON 3 (3–5 years) :
What options should I be creating - even if uncertain?
What bets cost little today but matter greatly later?
BALANCE AUDIT           :
What % of my time/energy goes to each horizon now?
What is the right allocation given my stage?
What would I need to stop doing in H1 to fund H2?
proTip:
The most common Three Horizons failure is treating H3 as a vision exercise and H1 as the
only real work. H3 options are built through small, cheap bets made consistently over
time. Amazon's AWS was an H3 bet in 2003 when their core H1 business was books. The
value of H3 is not in the vision — it is in the options it creates.
